memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get
maggots in it. 'Eat it today,' Moses said, 'because today is a sabbath to the
LORD. You will not find any of it on the ground today. Six days you are to
gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will not be any.'"
- Ex 16:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same manna. Kept overnight on an ordinary day, it bred maggots. Kept
overnight before the Sabbath, it stayed fresh.

This makes something clear: the spoiling was never about the food. It was about
obedience. When God said keep it, it kept. When God said do not keep it, it
rotted.

The difference was not in the manna but in the instruction.

That is a helpful principle for the Christian life. The same action can be
faithful in one context and faithless in another. Saving money can be wisdom or
it can be fear. Speaking up can be courage or it can be pride. Staying quiet can
be gentleness or it can be cowardice.

What matters is not simply the outward act but whether we are doing what God has
actually said to us.

Notice too the promise about the seventh day: "there will not be any." God tells
them in advance so they need not go out looking anxiously. He removes the
uncertainty that would spoil the rest.

He does not just command rest. He arranges the conditions for it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you are doing that is right in itself but wrong for you
   right now?
2. What uncertainty is stopping you from resting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me not just to do right things but to do what You are actually asking
of me. Settle my heart so I can rest. Amen.
